findings.evidence_excerpt: A task cannot name HUMAN as reviewer while naming coordinator as acceptance owner without an explicit authority rule explaining the two decisions.
findings.claim: Section 12 item 7 permits a task to name the coordinator as acceptance owner (with HUMAN as reviewer) whenever an 'explicit authority rule' exists, so a rule declared below HUMAN authority can transfer a deliverable-acceptance decision that the pinned authority reserves to an attributable HUMAN decision owner.
findings.impact: Acceptance evidence could be produced by the coordinator under a rule the design does not require to come from the HUMAN, contradicting the design's own constraint that the Coordinator must not own HUMAN acceptance (line 78) and the pinned authority that HUMAN exclusively owns deliverable acceptance; the design's own materiality rule (line 339) classifies any permission for a non-HUMAN artifact to grant authority as material.
findings.recommended_action: Delete the escape hatch and state that the acceptance owner is always the attributable HUMAN decision owner bound to the exact WBS hash; if a different acceptor is ever intended, require a separately recorded HUMAN authority decision before admission instead of a task-declared rule.

findings.evidence_excerpt: The GAT proposal remains higher authority for HUMAN decisions and Working-AIP/Workspace boundaries.
findings.claim: The design asserts a higher-authority role for the GAT proposal, which declares itself an inactive proposal that is 'not authority', while the pinned repo precedence order places AIP_PLAN/EXEC above guidelines, skills, wiki and workspace and recognizes source-of-truth canonical knowledge as authoritative, so the stated authority chain contradicts the pinned Source-of-Truth precedence.
findings.impact: A later WBS builder or governance reviewer could treat unapproved proposal text as binding over AIP-EXEC-009 and the Workspace, or justify or block control-plane changes on non-authority, weakening the precedence order that admission must obey.
findings.recommended_action: Restate subordination in repo precedence terms (Truth/canonical source_of_truth, SOP, Contract, AIP_PLAN/EXEC, guidelines, skills, wiki, workspace) and mark the GAT proposal as inactive non-authoritative design intent with only approved HUMAN decisions binding above this design.

findings.evidence_excerpt: the mission-specific contingency reserve is **two attempts** until council or HUMAN selects another explicit amount
findings.claim: Section 7.1 names 'council' alongside HUMAN as an entity that may select a different contingency reserve amount, so a review body is given a setting decision that P12 (line 191) and Section 16 (line 347) assign to the HUMAN decision owner.
findings.impact: The operative attempt reserve could be settled by a council output instead of an attributable HUMAN ceiling/reallocation decision, and a later WBS could cite the design's two-attempt value as if HUMAN policy had already been selected, weakening the HUMAN-authority requirement for ceiling and reallocation.
findings.recommended_action: Replace 'council or HUMAN' with 'the HUMAN decision owner', state that council output may only recommend a value, and state that no WBS may be built or admitted until the HUMAN selection at line 347 is recorded and bound to the WBS revision and hash.

findings.evidence_excerpt: Exact argv/cwd paths resolve; required effect backend is currently available; prohibited effects remain denied
findings.claim: P7's mandatory evidence and its single failure disposition omit the root/task allowed-command union membership check that Section 11 declares part of capability preflight (line 271), so a command that resolves, whose backend is available and that is not prohibited can satisfy P7 while being absent from the task's authorized command union.
findings.impact: The confirmed E-04 defect class (a required deliverable's owning command absent from the task's allowed commands) can still pass the invariant that gates charge, so schema-plus-semantic closure is not enforced at admission.
findings.recommended_action: Add union membership to P7's mandatory evidence (exact command appears in the pinned root/task allowed-command union, with the union source recorded and hashed), or declare it as a separate invariant with its own receipt and NOT_READY disposition.

findings.evidence_excerpt: Required independent routes/capabilities and one typed fallback are reserved; Chairman separation where council applies
findings.claim: P11 and Section 12.2 (line 280) require reviewers to be 'reserved' but define no reservation primitive, owning command, hold lifetime, expiry or release, and the only capability vocabulary the design defines is available/denied/unavailable/not_probed (line 273), so a reachability probe can be recorded as the reviewer_reservation receipt (line 171) and P11 passes without any capacity actually held.
findings.impact: The claim that review capacity is proven before charge is unverifiable, concurrent tasks may be admitted against the same routes, and implementers must either assert an unproven receipt or invent the reservation mechanism that the non-goals bar.
findings.recommended_action: Either define the reservation primitive with owning command, evidence fields, hold lifetime, expiry, release and the fail state when it cannot be established, or replace P11 with an availability probe plus the Section 12.4 typed fallback and record the double-booking residual risk explicitly.

findings.evidence_excerpt: One coordinator identity; no predecessor, agent or job can still write; `active_work` reconciled
findings.claim: P8 requires admission to establish that no predecessor, agent or job 'can still write', but the declared evidence form is a coordinator-assembled hash receipt with no named owning inspection tool, snapshot semantics or expiry, so the invariant is either an unprovable assertion or requires a locking mechanism that the non-goals exclude.
findings.impact: The 'mechanically closed' admission claim (line 128) does not hold for the quiescence surface, and a predecessor session or job can write after admission, reproducing the contradictory-state failure the design exists to prevent.
findings.recommended_action: Restate P8 as an observable snapshot condition (enumerate every mission-bound session and job with identity and stop evidence at commit, NOT_READY when enumeration is impossible), name the owning command and receipt fields, and define the fail state for each enumeration outcome.

findings.evidence_excerpt: 8. Run strict validator and execution-backed progress rendering on the exact candidate bytes.
findings.claim: The migration protocol states only pass conditions (Section 9.3, line 244) and gives no failure disposition, owner or recovery action for a step 8 validator/report failure or a step 9 review rejection after the transform, while Section 14's recovery matrix covers charge-time failures only.
findings.impact: A failed migration leaves no declared owner or next action against the acceptance-bearing ledger, so the strict-validator gate and the reversibility requirement are asserted rather than controlled.
findings.recommended_action: Add explicit dispositions for step 8 and step 9 failure (stop, retain original bytes and hash, restore the recorded pre-migration bytes through a named owning command, re-run the same validator, record no selection) and name the owner of each action.

findings.evidence_excerpt: The evidence-bound failure model is recorded at `.ai-work/workspaces/hoinv/TASK-20260915-control-plane-stabilization-design/04_findings.md#failure-model`.
findings.claim: Section 2 cites its evidence basis only as a mutable Workspace path with no content hash or revision, although the design hash-pins every admission input and promises evidence a later WBS can cite literally, so the root-cause classification cannot be re-verified against the bytes that supported it.
findings.impact: The requirement that the root cause be supported by pinned evidence holds only inside this review packet, not in the design itself, and a later reader cannot distinguish the evidence actually used from a subsequent Workspace edit.
findings.recommended_action: Pin the failure-model artifact's raw sha256 and revision in Section 2 and require the Section 16 handoff source list to carry that hash with an integrity check before admission.

rejected_candidates.reason: Rejected: the design does not invent a scheduler, daemon, custom WBS runner or new runtime service; Section 3.2 non-goals exclude them and Section 6 states the AdmissionBundle is an evidence artifact, not a runtime service.

Rejected: no charge is permitted in FROZEN, PREPARING, NOT_READY, READY or EXPIRED (line 128), and Section 5.2 with Section 14 preserves post-charge interruptions as charged failures instead of claiming rollback.
Rejected: migration is backup-first (Section 9.2 step 1 copies exact pre-migration bytes and records SHA-256) and Section 9.3 forbids any task becoming accepted or ready solely because of migration.
Rejected: schema validation is not treated as sufficient; P2 and Section 8 require a closed semantic command-to-deliverable closure matrix in addition to the official format receipt.

Rejected: manual ASC transitions are not permitted as satisfying evidence; Section 10 forbids manual ASC body edits as acceptance evidence and requires the declared run_aip.py argv, which P6 verifies as producing the fresh ASC.
Rejected: the AdmissionBundle is not claimed to grant execution authority; Section 5.1 and Section 17 state that READY and a council pass are not authority to execute.
